name: Fort Sumter relief expedition
notes: Fox, a man without a post, commands the troops and stores (OR I-1 p. 235; ORN I-4 pp. 245 to 248). Opened by S01's provision_notice (0040).

name: Department of Virginia (Fort Monroe)
notes: [I] effective appointment by the history rule seat on 22 May 1861: Scott to Butler, 18 May, Butler Correspondence I pp. 94-95; Butler to Scott, 24 May, ibid. p. 104 and OR I-2 p. 648 (Wednesday arrival, 22 May). Dimick retains the regular garrison. Temporary department representation remains a 1B stand-in; no calendar notice opens it.

name: Troops near Harpers Ferry
notes: OR I-2 pp.844-845 (15 May assignment), p.470 (assumed command 23 May), p.856 (18 May, President intends army here). [I] Declared command opened by the doctrine appointment; no opening force and no forced battle. Requires Virginia on the Confederate side and Johnston eligible through the service owner. S1: OR I-2 p.470 dates actual assumption to 23 May. [I] The rule-seat opening now waits for that effective date, his ordinary resignation and Virginia's side, rather than opening on the May 15 assignment order. S90 [I]: the operational order channel runs through the Adjutant and Inspector General. July 17-18 correspondence is issued by Cooper and answered to him (OR I-II pp.478,980-982); this does not make the Secretary of War an additional resisting relay on the same dispatch. The War Department affiliation and separate state requisitions remain.

name: Alexandria line (headquarters at Manassas)
notes: OR I-2 p.896, Special Orders 149, 31 May; pp.901-902, Beauregard 3 June, arrival 1 June. [I] Declared command opened by the rule-seat assignment, with normal delivery latency. Only the commander leaves Charleston; troops require separate transfers and joining marches. S90 [I]: the operational order channel runs through the Adjutant and Inspector General. July 17-18 correspondence is issued by Cooper and answered to him (OR I-II pp.478,980-982); this does not make the Secretary of War an additional resisting relay on the same dispatch. The War Department affiliation and separate state requisitions remain.

name: Department of Pennsylvania
notes: GO12 section 3, 27 April 1861, p.31, and OR I-2 chronological summary p.1. [I] Declared, unopened command for the effective rule-seat appointment. Philadelphia is the order's headquarters; no opening force, calendar notice or forced campaign. Patterson's later service expiry is not implemented by this appointment.

name: Department of Northeastern Virginia
notes: GO26, 27 May 1861, p.61: Virginia east of the Alleghanies and north of James River, except Fort Monroe and sixty miles around it; headquarters movable. OR I-2 chronological summary p.2: assumes 28 May; pp.59-60: Arlington headquarters 1 June. [I] Arlington maps to northern_virginia; no opening troops and no forced battle. Temporary department representation is a 1A stand-in, as R89.

name: Superintendent of the Recruiting Service (Fort Columbus)
notes: GO12 section 4 p.31, 27 April, directs C.F.Smith to Fort Columbus to assume duties assigned in SO80 March 15. [I] The bureau reports through the Adjutant General; Fort Columbus maps to new_york. Declared but unopened, no opening force. Existing call, compliance, loyalty and muster owners represent the May 4 raising effort with unknown actual strength; a temporary office is the disclosed 1A representation.
